| Food Fraud | This Program is designed to assess put in place Economically-Motivated adulteration of food products and put in place proportional control meausres | GOPDC FSQM has considered all possible threats and has established threat assesment critical control points (TACCP). This also provides guidance on the avoidance and mitigation of threat to food and food supply. The possible risk associated with this Program includes: destruction of equipment and machinery,pilfering, intruders, delibrate contamination of food, fraud, extortion of money, attack by poachers, cyber crime, personnel security and disgrutled individual tampering , closing down the factory and food incident cases. | GOPDC has adopted Threat Assesment Critical Control points (TACCP)approach according to PAS 965: 2014 and has a team (trained security operatives and Food Safety Team), access control measures, survellance team, material and vehicle movement control documents, key registers. Also deployment of armed security personnel to vulnerable points, internal police post, issuing of visitors reflective jackets and documentation, changing facilities - seperate personal clothing from work wear and possitive identification of staff. Demacation and sign post have also been installed at restricted areas to control movement of persons. We also have corrective measures to tampering evidence ( seals on trucks), fire extinquisher installed all round the premises and offices to control fire outbreak. There is training of recruited security personnel on access control of people and vehicles in and out of the factory. site plans and processing details are controlled. 7.2.3 Personnel Security Measures 7.2.3.1 Personnel security is taken seriously. Measures have been put in place to ensure that only authorized personnel are on the factory premises at any point in time. This includes visitors on site. 7.2.3.2 This establishment has in place at least one of the following measures for personnel security; 7.2.3.2.1 Employee Security 7.2.3.2.1.1 During hiring of employees, thorough background checks are done. 7.2.3.2.1.2 Employees are trained to know what they can do on site. 7.2.3.2.1.3 Areas restricted to be accessed by only a category of employees is made known to every employee hired. 7.2.3.2.1.4 Confidentiality clauses are inserted into employment letters. Employees are made to sign the confidentiality agreement. 7.2.3.2.2 Non-employee Security 7.2.3.2.2.1 Provision has been made for non-employees such as visitors, guests, customers, contractors, suppliers, third party drivers etc. 7.2.3.2.2.2 A log of non-employees entering the establishment is maintained at the main security area. 7.2.3.2.2.3 A visitor’s ID card has been designed with numbers and these are assigned to every visitor who enters the facility to conduct one business or the other. 7.2.3.2.2.4 All visitors are mandated to wear their visitor ID cards where they would be very visible. 7.2.3.2.2.5 Non-employees are chaperoned on-site by security or the person they came to transact business with and they are basically restricted to designated areas of the factory. 7.2.3.2.2.6 Non-employees have restrictions on what they can do on site. site plans and processing details are controlled. 7.2.3 Personnel Security Measures 7.2.3.1 Personnel security is taken seriously. Measures have been put in place to ensure that only authorized personnel are on the factory premises at any point in time. This includes visitors on site. 7.2.3.2 This establishment has in place at least one of the following measures for personnel security; 7.2.3.2.1 Employee Security 7.2.3.2.1.1 During hiring of employees, thorough background checks are done. 7.2.3.2.1.2 Employees are trained to know what they can do on site. 7.2.3.2.1.3 Areas restricted to be accessed by only a category of employees is made known to every employee hired. 7.2.3.2.1.4 Confidentiality clauses are inserted into employment letters. Employees are made to sign the confidentiality agreement. 7.2.3.2.2 Non-employee Security 7.2.3.2.2.1 Provision has been made for non-employees such as visitors, guests, customers, contractors, suppliers, third party drivers etc. 7.2.3.2.2.2 A log of non-employees entering the establishment is maintained at the main security area. 7.2.3.2.2.3 A visitor’s ID card has been designed with numbers and these are assigned to every visitor who enters the facility to conduct one business or the other. 7.2.3.2.2.4 All visitors are mandated to wear their visitor ID cards where they would be very visible. 7.2.3.2.2.5 Non-employees are chaperoned on-site by security or the person they came to transact business with and they are basically restricted to designated areas of the factory. 7.2.3.2.2.6 Non-employees have restrictions on what they can do on site. For instance, non-employees are not permitted to take pictures on site. 7.2.3.2.3 Security Training 7.2.3.2.3.1 All new employees undergo security awareness training. Existing employees undergo periodic security awareness training. 7.2.3.2.3.2 Employees are trained on access control, handling of sensitive information, what suspicious activities look like and reporting such activities to management or the security team. 7.2.4 Incident Response Security Measures. 7.2.4.1 An incident response security references the incident management plan already in place. | Food Fraud | This Program is designed to assess put in place Economically-Motivated adulteration of food products and put in place proportional control meausres | GOPDC FSQM has considered all possible threats and has established threat assesment critical control points (TACCP). This also provides guidance on the avoidance and mitigation of threat to food and food supply. The possible risk associated with this Program includes: destruction of equipment and machinery,pilfering, intruders, delibrate contamination of food, fraud, extortion of money, attack by poachers, cyber crime, personnel security and disgrutled individual tampering , closing down the factory and food incident cases. | GOPDC has adopted Threat Assesment Critical Control points (TACCP)approach according to PAS 965: 2014 and has a team (trained security operatives and Food Safety Team), access control measures, survellance team, material and vehicle movement control documents, key registers. Also deployment of armed security personnel to vulnerable points, internal police post, issuing of visitors reflective jackets and documentation, changing facilities - seperate personal clothing from work wear and possitive identification of staff. Demacation and sign post have also been installed at restricted areas to control movement of persons. We also have corrective measures to tampering evidence ( seals on trucks), fire extinquisher installed all round the premises and offices to control fire outbreak. There is training of recruited security personnel on access control of people and vehicles in and out of the factory. Related necessary plans/procedures such as product recalls/withdrawals and personnel emergency or evacuation procedures are in place and effective Employees, contractors as well as visitors are identified by appropriate form of ID card or other appropriate means (Reflectors) The factory is securely fenced to prevent unauthorized entry of people and vehicles. There is placement of notices at the security gate or entrance which will direct visitors and unauthorized persons into the factory (visitors’ policy). Security cameras are in placed at high security risk areas in the factory eg. Refinery stearin melting tanks, filling plant, warehouses, product storage tanks, water treatment and where applicable continuous monitoring by an attendant and/or a security personnel. Measures have been put in place to ensure that only authorized personnel are on the factory premises at any point in time. This includes visitors on site. 7.2.3.2 This establishment has in place at least one of the following measures for personnel security; 7.2.3.2.1 Employee Security 7.2.3.2.1.1 During hiring of employees, thorough background checks are done. 7.2.3.2.1.2 Employees are trained to know what they can do on site. 7.2.3.2.1.3 Areas restricted to be accessed by only a category of employees is made known to every employee hired. 7.2.3.2.1.4 Confidentiality clauses are inserted into employment letters. Employees are made to sign the confidentiality agreement. 7.2.3.2.2 Non-employee Security 7.2.3.2.2.1 Provision has been made for non-employees such as visitors, guests, customers, contractors, suppliers, third party drivers etc. 7.2.3.2.2.2 A log of non-employees entering the establishment is maintained at the main security area. 7.2.3.2.2.3 A visitor’s ID card has been designed with numbers and these are assigned to every visitor who enters the facility to conduct one business or the other. 7.2.3.2.2.4 All visitors are mandated to wear their visitor ID cards where they would be very visible. 7.2.3.2.2.5 Non-employees are chaperoned on-site by security or the person they came to transact business with and they are basically restricted to designated areas of the factory. 7.2.3.2.2.6 Non-employees have restrictions on what they can do on site. For instance, non-employees are not permitted to take pictures on site. 7.2.3.2.3 Security Training 7.2.3.2.3.1 All new employees undergo security awareness training. Existing employees undergo periodic security awareness training. 7.2.3.2.3.2 Employees are trained on access control, handling of sensitive information, what suspicious activities look like and reporting such activities to management or the security team. 7.2.4 Incident Response Security Measures. 7.2.4.1 An incident response security references the incident management plan already in place. This also provides guidance on the avoidance and mitigation of threat to food and food supply. The possible risk associated with this Program includes: destruction of equipment and machinery,pilfering, intruders, delibrate contamination of food, fraud, extortion of money, attack by poachers, cyber crime, personnel security and disgrutled individual tampering , closing down the factory and food incident cases. | GOPDC has adopted Threat Assesment Critical Control points (TACCP)approach according to PAS 965: 2014 and has a team (trained security operatives and Food Safety Team), access control measures, survellance team, material and vehicle movement control documents, key registers. Also deployment of armed security personnel to vulnerable points, internal police post, issuing of visitors reflective jackets and documentation, changing facilities - seperate personal clothing from work wear and possitive identification of staff. Demacation and sign post have also been installed at restricted areas to control movement of persons. We also have corrective measures to tampering evidence ( seals on trucks), fire extinquisher installed all round the premises and offices to control fire outbreak. There is training of recruited security personnel on access control of people and vehicles in and out of the factory. controlled, administered and audited, and subject to central management review; - An internal audit has been conducted on each site within one year prior to certification; - Following the certification, an internal audit shall be carried out on each site within the certification period. The internal audit shall comply with ISO 22000. - Audit findings of the individual sites shall be considered indicative of the entire system and correction shall be implemented accordingly. - For Organizations with 20 sites or less, multi-site sampling is not allowed. Each site must be audited at each activity. FSSC Multi-site sampling is only possible for categories A, E, FI, G and for organizations with more than 20 sites operating similar processes within these categories. Where multi-site sampling is permitted the following apply; - A sampling plan shall be utilized to ensure an effective audit of the FSMS - The sampling plan for more than 20 sites shall be at the ration of 1 site per 5 sites with a minimum of 20. - The sites shall be randomly selected and after the audit, non-sampled sites may be nonconforming (i.e. not meeting certification thresholds for ISO 22000). - Evaluation of the audit findings of the sampled sites shall be deemed equivalent to the internal audit findings of the same site. - At least annually, an audit of the central FSMS shall be performed - At least annually, surveillance audits shall be performed on the required number of sampled sites. Measures have been put in place to ensure that only authorized personnel are on the factory premises at any point in time. This includes visitors on site. 7.2.3.2 This establishment has in place at least one of the following measures for personnel security; 7.2.3.2.1 Employee Security 7.2.3.2.1.1 During hiring of employees, thorough background checks are done. 7.2.3.2.1.2 Employees are trained to know what they can do on site. 7.2.3.2.1.3 Areas restricted to be accessed by only a category of employees is made known to every employee hired. 7.2.3.2.1.4 Confidentiality clauses are inserted into employment letters. Where multi-site sampling is permitted the following apply; - A sampling plan shall be utilized to ensure an effective audit of the FSMS - The sampling plan for more than 20 sites shall be at the ration of 1 site per 5 sites with a minimum of 20. - The sites shall be randomly selected and after the audit, non-sampled sites may be nonconforming (i.e. not meeting certification thresholds for ISO 22000). - Evaluation of the audit findings of the sampled sites shall be deemed equivalent to the internal audit findings of the same site. - At least annually, an audit of the central FSMS shall be performed - At least annually, surveillance audits shall be performed on the required number of sampled sites. lights erected along the perimeter fencing for visibility at night and to ward off any person or group of people who may have ulterior motives. 7.2.1.3.1.3 The entire facility is periodically monitored by the security for suspicious activity. 7.2.1.3.1.4 Doors are locked after work and windows and all other openings are secured. 7.2.1.3.2 Shipping/Receiving Security 7.2.1.3.2.1 Incoming raw materials and packaging materials are inspected for potential tampering. 7.2.1.3.2.2 Each vehicle coming to offload and those leaving the premises for outside warehouses and distribution centers are always inspected for suspicious activity. One measure to ensure safety of incoming and outgoing materials is ensuring that suppliers secure loads with seals. 7.2.1.3.2.3 All trucks leaving the factory with finished products or packaging materials for outside storage are sealed/or shrink-wrapped. 7.2.1.3.3 Mail Handling Security 7.2.1.3.3.1 All parcels and letters coming through the mail or hand-delivered are handled away from the production floor, canteen, finished goods warehouse, packaging stores and any other place on site which is close to products, packaging or the production areas. 7.2.1.3.3.1 All employees who handle mail are trained on bioterrorism and how to handle items of external origin. 7.2.2. Inside Security Measures 7.2.2.1 Measures are taken within the perimeter including offices and production areas to ensure security is maintained. 7.2.2.2 Access control has been incorporated into door lock systems to give access to only authorized persons to specific areas of the factory. 7.2.2.3 Signs have been posted at areas to clearly communicate restricted access status. The main purpose of these activities is to protect product from intentional contamination. 7.2.2.4 Access to the raw paper storage and printing inks for instance is restricted. All access points are locked and only authorized personnel have access to it. 7.2.2.5 This establishment has in place at least one of the following measures for inside security. 7.2.2.5.1 General Inside Security 7.2.2.5.1.1 Any parcel that raises suspicion is reported to the security team. 7.2.2.5.1.2 All restricted areas within the factory are clearly identified and labelled as such. 7.2.2.5.1.3 Any material which is suspected not to have been previously inspected is quarantined for thorough inspection before use.

|  | HAZARD ANALYSIS | Each potential hazard is listed and significance is determined with help of severity of health effect and likelihood of occurrence |

| HACCP PLAN /oPRP PLAN |  | List and Overview of all identified CCPs and oPRPs with control measures, limits, corrective actions and responsibilities |

This includes visitors on site. 7.2.3.2 This establishment has in place at least one of the following measures for personnel security; 7.2.3.2.1 Employee Security 7.2.3.2.1.1 During hiring of employees, thorough background checks are done. 7.2.3.2.1.2 Employees are trained to know what they can do on site. 7.2.3.2.1.3 Areas restricted to be accessed by only a category of employees is made known to every employee hired. 7.2.3.2.1.4 Confidentiality clauses are inserted into employment letters. Employees are made to sign the confidentiality agreement. 7.2.3.2.2 Non-employee Security 7.2.3.2.2.1 Provision has been made for non-employees such as visitors, guests, customers, contractors, suppliers, third party drivers etc. 7.2.3.2.2.2 A log of non-employees entering the establishment is maintained at the main security area. 7.2.3.2.2.3 A visitor’s ID card has been designed with numbers and these are assigned to every visitor who enters the facility to conduct one business or the other. 7.2.3.2.2.4 All visitors are mandated to wear their visitor ID cards where they would be very visible. 7.2.3.2.2.5 Non-employees are chaperoned on-site by security or the person they came to transact business with and they are basically restricted to designated areas of the factory. 7.2.3.2.2.6 Non-employees have restrictions on what they can do on site. For instance, non-employees are not permitted to take pictures on site. 7.2.3.2.3 Security Training 7.2.3.2.3.1 All new employees undergo security awareness training. Existing employees undergo periodic security awareness training. 7.2.3.2.3.2 Employees are trained on access control, handling of sensitive information, what suspicious activities look like and reporting such activities to management or the security team. 7.2.4 Incident Response Security Measures. 7.2.4.1 An incident response security references the incident management plan already in place. The idea is to respond quickly to a product contamination threat or event using planned measures. 7.2.4.2 There is already an existing incident management plan which deals with product recalls whether it is food safety related or quality

| FS_PRP_06 | Management of Purchased materials and services | This PRP describes the selection of suppliers for the supply of the types of raw and packaging materials purchased for production and how they are received and stored in the factory. | Procurement of materials and services for use in production must be managed in order to control food safety risks to food packing. | 1.0 Selection and management of suppliers 1.1.1 To ensure the right supplier is selected a hazard assessment, including the potential risk to the final product is used to justify the decision to engage a particular supplier.  1.1.2 The following is done; 1.1.2.1 Assess the supplier’s ability to meet quality and food safety expectations, requirements and specifications.  1.1.2.2 Some of the procedures used for assessing suppliers include; 1.1.2.2.1 Audit of the supplying site prior to accepting materials for production or the provision of relevant certifications or desktop audit.  1.1.2.2.2 Appropriate third-party certification.  1.1.2.2.3 Performance monitoring of the supplier to assure continued approval status. 1.1.2.2.4 Suppliers will be contacted on their performance and be required to reply especially to non-conformances that involves product quality  1.2 Incoming material requirements (raw/ingredients/packaging) 1.2.1 All delivery vehicles are checked prior to, and during, offloading to verify that the quality and safety of the material has been maintained during transit.  1.2.2 All delivered materials are tested and or covered by COA to verify conformity with specified requirements prior to acceptance or use. The method of verification is documented for each item delivered by suppliers.  1.3.3 The inspection frequency is based on the hazard presented by the material and the risk assessment of the specific suppliers.  1.3.4 All non-conforming products are placed on-hold and rejected to be returned back to the supplier. 1.3.5 In cases where purchased items are imported, the supplier is notified of the non-conformance after which the material is either sold to recycling plants in the case of packaging or destroyed under supervision in the case of other items which cannot be recycled. 1.3.6 Criteria for disqualification: 1.3.6.1 Lack of prompt response to complaint or problem identify by the suppliers. 1.3.6.2 Lack of supply of quality raw material in two successions without corrective actions.  1.3.7 All items purchased are stored in demarcated storage areas and released to production for use. | Daily, monthly and anually | Factory Manager, Warehouse Manager, | FS/PRP 06/REC 05 - Approved Suppliers and Service Providers' List  Material Intake Checklist                  FS/PRP 06/FORM 01 – Supplier Monitoring/Tracking sheet     FS/PRP 06/FORM 02 -  Suppliers/Questionnaire Evaluation Form Internal Audit Reports |  | Chemical contamination |  | Procedure for handling and storing food and non-food materials. |

| FS_PRP_09 | PRP for Pest Control | This PRP outlines the methods that is employed to control all potential pests on the premises of the factory. It details out the specific functions of pest control companies in accessing, executing eradication strategies and ensuring no dead pests are left on site. | A programme to be implemented to prevent risks to food safety in the production halls, offices, the canteen and the entire premises including external surroundings used for food packaging production. | 7.1 Introduction 7.1.1 Poly Products recognizes the need to control pests. These include rodents, snakes, flying and crawling insects and other pests. Hence pest control is an integral part of the organization’s activities.  7.1.2 Areas included in the pest control program are the production areas, offices, warehouses, canteen, stores and the general factory site and its immediate surroundings.  7.1.3 This is done on a regular basis to prevent contamination of products and food contact surfaces.  7.1.4 Poly Products shall engage the services of a qualified pest control agency/contractor to undertake the activity of controlling pests on site. In order to ensure a professional job, Poly Products shall ensure the pest control accredited agency is a registered company by law.   7.2 General Factory There shall be regular at least monthly spraying of the factory against mosquitoes, snakes and other crawling and flying insects. Pesticides shall be employed in this exercise.  7.3 Production Hall 7.3.1 Specific areas in the production hall shall be identified. These areas shall have traps to control rodents.  7.3.2 Insectocutors (special electrical equipment for killing flying insects) shall be installed for the control of insects and flies.  7.4 Offices Periodic disinfection and spraying of insecticides shall be done in offices as per the pest control schedule. All offices shall also have pest traps to control rodents where applicable.   7.5 Warehouses/Stores 7.5.1 All warehouses and stores for raw materials, packaging materials and finished goods shall be fitted with pest traps to control the activities of rodents.  7.5.2 These traps as well as those in other areas on the pest map shall be inspected on a weekly basis except weekends, holidays.  7.5.3 The purpose of this inspection is to pick up any dead rodents for disposal and subsequent replacement of baits, glue-boards as applicable.   7.6 Canteen 7.6.1 The presence of food residue and transient garbage makes the canteen susceptible to pest invasion, especially houseflies, cockroaches and rodents.   7.6.2 Rodent traps shall be placed at possible entry points in the canteen to control rodents. Insectocutors would be installed in the canteen to control houseflies.  7.6.3 Aerosols shall not be permitted in the canteen in order to avoid contamination of food.  7.6.4 The canteen shall be included in the periodic fumigation activity in order to control mosquitoes and cockroaches. All utensils and kitchen equipment including food contact surfaces shall be covered during the fumigation activity. After fumigation, utensils, equipment and food contact surfaces shall be washed and disinfected.  7.7 Approved Chemicals 7.7.1 The pest control contractor shall be asked to present all chemicals to be used for controlling pests on site together with the MSDS.  7.7.2 This shall include chemicals used to control mosquitoes, snakes, mice, rats and other rodents. It is the responsibility of the Food Safety Team Leader to clear all chemicals before application.  7.7.3 As a general rule, canteen and food packaging areas like production areas shall be covered before fumigation exercise irrespective of what chemical it is.  7.7.4 Surfaces and equipment shall be cleaned and disinfected in such peculiar cases.  7.7.5 Physical traps shall include the use of secured bait traps and/or adhesives. The traps and or adhesives shall be placed at each of the bait stations identified.   7.7.6 Pest control agents, cleaners shall inspect the traps on a weekly basis whether any rodent or any other pest has been caught. If there is a rodent trapped, the pest would be picked up and disposed correctly. If it was the cleaner that sighted the pest, the pest control agents will be notified.  7.7.7 If there are no rodents, the personnel checks whether the secured bait is still there or not and if not a new bait is replaced  7.7.8 The Pest Control Agent shall submit monthly reports indicating all activities on site.  7.7.9 The report shall include the type of pesticides used, quantity, concentration used, where, when and how applied, target pests, number of pest traps replaced (if any).  7.8 Trigger Levels 7.8.1 The following activity below will serve as a trigger for the immediate intervention of an external pest controller. The threshold level that will necessitate a trigger are 7.8.1.1 An increase in pest activity in a particular area, or as observed in the pest trend activity report or a sighting of a snake should trigger the intervention of an external pest controller 7.8.1.2 a sighting of a live rat, lizard or reptile within the production hall 7.8.1.3 a sighting of a snake anywhere within the premises 7.8.1.4 any unusual pest activity sighted anywhere on site 7.8.1.5 a spike in pest control trends    7.9 Corrective and Preventative Actions 7.9.1 In the event of a spike in pest trend activity or any of the activity that can trigger as listed in 7.8 above, there should be a documented steps or corrective actions to be taking using the following format as below | Daily, weekly or monthly | Pest Controller, SHE Officer, Food Safety Team Leader | FS/PRP 09/REC 01 Pest Control Report.   FS/PRP 09/ATTACH 01: Pest Map Layout Contract for Pest Control Contractor  Certificate for Pest Control Contractor      FS/PRP 09/REC 02 Pest Control Trend Activity    FS/PRP 09/REC 03 Pesticide Usage Log    FS/PRP 09/REC 04 Bait Station Monitoring Record    FS/PRP 09/REC 05 Corrective Action Report     MSDS for Chemicals used in pest control FS/PRP 09/REC 01 Pest Control Report    FS/PRP 09/REC 02 Pest Control Trend Activity    FS/PRP 09/REC 03 Pesticide Usage Log    FS/PRP 09/REC 04 Bait Station Monitoring Record    FS/PRP 09/REC 05 Corrective Action Report     MSDS for Chemicals used in pest control |  | Pest control chemicals | Microbial contamintion. | FS_PRP_05 | Equipment Suitability, Cleaning & Maintenance | PRP for Equipement Suitabilty, Cleaning & Maintenance | The purpose of this PRP is to ensure that equipment used in production and packaging areas are designed to prevent contamination | 1.0 General Requirements 1.1 Poly Products Company Limited has provided equipment designed to prevent contamination for use in production of food packaging.  2.0  Hygiene Design and food contact surfaces 2.1 Poly Products Company Limited has taken into consideration the potential sources of contamination from equipment constructed with unsuitable material. 2.2 Therefore, all processing equipment are constructed from stainless steel and firm non-leaking and non-wearable plastic material. The construction materials compatible with the intended food packaging, lubricants and cleaning or flushing agents. 2.3 The food contact surfaces of the processing equipment are smooth, accessible and cleanable.  2.4  Equipment components containing metals of known toxicity (e.g. mercury) are excluded from use for the processing of food packaging.  3.0 Maintenance of Equipment  3.1 Poly Products Company Limited has in place a system of planned maintenance which covers all equipment.  3.2 Equipment maintenance programmes are available and systematically applied to minimize the potential for contamination of product by equipment.  3.3 A procedure has been established to remove any potential contaminant from machinery and equipment after maintenance work. Equipment with product contact surfaces after maintenance are released in accordance to line release protocols before being used by production.    3.4 Maintenance personnel are required to follow the prescribed procedures including, where appropriate, hygiene measures. Temporary engineering and modifications are avoided but strictly controlled when they are carried out. | Daily | Maintenance Engineer Food Safety Team Leader Factory Manager | FS/PRP05.01 – Equipment Calibration Schedule    FS/PRP 05.03 – Equipment Cleaning Record    FS_PRP_05 ATTACH 01 – Preventive Maintenance Plan    FS/PRP 01/CL 01 -Facility Inspection Checklist/Report    FS/PRP04.02 – Job Ticket    FS/PRP06/ATTACH01 – Stock Card | Dust and soil particles from environment. | Chemical contamination from lubricants, fuels and detergents. | Microbial contamination from personnel. | GMP protocols for personnel, cleaning and maintenance of equipment, pest control program, use of food grade lubricants and detergents. |

All these areas were considered during the HACCP study.  1.1.2 To control the likelihood of these hazards occurring, some control measures have been taking as a minimum.   1.1.2.1 The Quality Manager together with the Food Safety Team shall ensure to;  1.1.2.2 Separate non-food items from finished products.  1.1.2.3 Separate areas for the storage of raw materials and finished products. 1.1.2.4 Control access to process areas, the laboratory and any other area identified as medium risk. Only authorized staff are allowed to access such areas of production.  1.1.2.5 Streamline traffic patterns.  1.2 Allergen management 1.2.1 There are no allergens in the food packaging process. Poly Products Ltd has however put in place rigorous cleaning protocols to ensure there are no allergen cross-contact by cleaning agents.  1.2.2 All employees including maintenance staff involved in cleaning of equipment are trained in allergen awareness and associated manufacturing practices.  1.3 Physical contamination 1.3.1 Periodic inspections are done to ensure coverings of machines made of brittle materials such as machine covering made of Perspex and glass components of equipment are intact.   1.3.2 Regular monthly glass audits are carried out and measures put in place to prevent, control or detect potential contamination and corrective actions put in place.  1.3.3 The use of snap off knife blade is forbidden.  1.3.4 Tools are to be locked up in their respective tool boxes and must not be left loose in any place or on surfaces where product contamination can occur  1.4 Chemical contamination 1.4.1  Eliminate or prevent chemical contamination by ensuring that;  1.4.1.1 All lubricants employed in production are food grade.  1.4.1.2 Precautions are taken to ensure that lubricants do not enter into the product.  1.4.1.3 All lubricants are stored in a dedicated area far from the production hall to prevent accidental leakage into products. |  | Food Safety Team Leader, Quality Manager, Food Safety Team |  |  | FS/PRP 08/ATTACH 01 – Master Cleaning Plan     FS/PRP 05.02 – Filter Replacement Record     FS/PRP 07/REC 01 - Monthly Glass/Illumination Inspection Records     MSDS for all chemicals     IMS/WP 01.24/ATTACH 01 – Allergen Declaration GMP Protocols |  | Microbial contamination from personnel and pest. | 3 | Utilities | PRP for Utilities. | The PRP outlines the programmes that ensures that the organization is operating, maintaining and repairing components of the utility system to avoid contamination of products and to achieve efficiency in energy, water and air use. | 1.0 General Provisions 1.1 All factory buildings and facilities including utilities is managed in such a manner as to prevent contamination of products and processes. They are also managed in the most energy efficient manner without endangering the health and safety of employees.  1.2 Facilities Management will endeavour to take the necessary steps to provide an adequate, reliable, and cost-effective utilities infrastructure at all present and planned future buildings and facilities managed by the department. These shall be established in the most hygienic manner in order to ensure product safety.  1.3 The provision and distribution routes for utilities to and around processing and storage areas are designed to minimize the risk of product contamination. The quality of utilities is monitored to minimize product contamination risk.   2.0 Water Supply 2.1 Sufficient supply of potable water to meet the needs of production processes is assured. Facilities for storage and distribution of water have been designed to meet the quality requirements of water.  2.2 Poly Products uses water for washing and other cleaning activities. Potable water is sourced from the municipal water treatment plant. Approved water pipes have been used on site to connect water from the main municipal lines to preserve its quality and safety. Connections are hygienically done to prevent external contaminated water from flowing into the pipes in the event that water stops flowing from the treatment plant.  2.3 Periodic water analysis shall be done on an annual basis. See attachment FS/PRP 03/ATTACH 01 for the scope, frequency, sampling point etc. This activity is outsourced to the national laboratory or approved/recognized testing laboratory to carry out by taking water. The appropriate ISO method or other authorized standard for air count is employed in this exercise.   3.0 Air quality and ventilation 3.1 Air flowing from outside into the production space can be a source of bacteria and mould spores. Poly Products has considered this in the design of its ventilation system especially at the production hall. Hence there are no windows opening directly into the production areas.  3.2 Periodic air counts are done for each of the sections of production. See attachment FS/PRP 03/ATTACH 01 This activity is outsourced to the national laboratory or approved/recognized testing laboratory to carry out. Prepared media in petri dishes are exposed in various sections of production for some minutes. Dishes are incubated and the total viable count results are analyzed. The appropriate ISO method or other authorized standard for air count is employed in this exercise.   4.0 Compressed air and other gases 4.1 Compressed air (which are from in-built vacuum pumps) used in the production process have been constructed and maintained so as to prevent direct contact products and the packaging.  4.2 Maintenance of the compressed air system is part of the site maintenance schedule. Maintenance shall include checking and cleaning of filters and replacement of filters if necessary.   5.0 Lighting 5.1 Adequate lighting has been provided in all production and storage areas to allow personnel to operate in a hygienic manner.   5.2 All lights in both critical and non-critical areas are covered to catch fragments of glass in case of lamp breakage.   5.3 Maintenance work on lighting is done in such a way as to prevent contamination of products. Light bulb replacement shall be done during weekend shutdown maintenance periods and not in the course of production.  5.4 Indoor lighting will be reduced in number and / or wattage, wherever possible, to provide for the minimum but adequate lighting levels consistent with the needs of the programs and functions being provided in those spaces, and with any state-mandated standards for the efficient and effective use of those spaces.  5.5 For efficient use of energy, the rooftop including production and storage areas are equipped with transparent roof for sunlight illumination during daytime.   5.6 Outside lighting on building exteriors and loading bay shall be maintained at the brightness levels necessary to provide appropriate security and safety on the facility’s grounds, parking lots, and building entrances. | Daily, weekly, monthly, etc. | Maintenance Manager, Factory Manager, Food Safety Team Leade and Departmental heads. | FS/PRP 03/ATTACH 01 - Plan/Schedule for Water, Air, Swab Analysis | Dust and soil contamination from environment. |  | Microbial contamination form air and water. Eg Legionella | Water potability analyses of water sources used in the factory. |

| FS_PRP_13 | PRP for Storage & Transport | This PRP is to outline the total management of all finished goods warehouses. | The storage and transportation of finished food packaging must be managed to control food safety hazards. | 7.1 Introduction 7.1.1 Management of products before they are shipped to customers is crucial. The quality and safety of products must be preserved within the warehouse before delivery to customers and to general trade. 7.1.2 Poly Products Ltd therefore ensures that the best standards are put in place to assure the appropriate storage and distribution of its products including good house-keeping. 7.2 Warehouse Requirements 7.2.1 General 7.2.1.1 There is a dedicated person in charge of all warehouses to manage and administer the goods kept there. 7.2.1.2 This includes stock rotation, quantity and quarantine (segregation) of non-conforming stock, damaged stock, rejected stock and returned stock. The dedicated person is also responsible for blocking and releasing of goods. 7.2.2 Storage Area 7.2.2.1 The storage area is located within the factory of Poly Products Ltd. 7.2.2.2 The storage area is in a dedicated area that promote the hygiene and safety of the products stored in them. 7.2.2.3 They are not located close to sources of infection. 7.2.2.4 Standards maintained for warehouses within the factory shall be extended to warehouses located outside the factory premises (if necessary). 7.2.2.5 Such warehouses must not be located close to possible sources of infection such as 7.2.2.5.1 Flood prone areas 7.2.2.5.2 Refuse dumps 7.2.2.5.3 Public toilets 7.2.2.5.4 Dusty areas 7.2.2.5.5 Choked gutters 7.2.2.6 In addition to these, warehouses must; 7.2.2.6.1 not be sited close to chemical factories where the possibility of taint is high. 7.2.2.6.2 have roadways that have hard surfaces, suitable for wheeled traffic and adequately drained. 7.2.2.6.3 have suitable drainage systems to prevent rainwater from entering into the warehouse. 7.2.2.6.4 be designed for safe traffic flow 7.2.2.6.5 have access controlled. 7.2.3 Building and facilities 7.2.3.1 The storage area has been designed to permit easy and adequate cleaning. 7.2.3.2 Dust control was considered in the design to ensure products are not covered in dust. 7.2.3.3 The storage

| 4 | Waste Disposal | PRP for Waste Disposal | The purpose of this PRP is to outline the procedure for managing waste on site to maintain a sanitary/clean environment necessary for the production of products of the highest quality and safety. | 1.0 General requirements Poly Products Ltd has put systems in place to ensure that waste materials are identified, collected, removed and disposed in a manner which prevents contamination of products and production areas.  2.0 Types of Waste The types of waste generated at Poly Products Ltd are categorized as; 2.1 Plastic waste-flexible films 2.2 General waste including packages of consumables, food debris from canteen and other office supplies 2.3 Liquid waste from toilet facilities and the main amenities.    3.0 Containers for waste, inedible or hazardous substances 3.1 The following standards and guidelines are put in place regarding containers for waste and inedible or hazardous substances:  3.1.1 Containers are clearly identified for their various intended purposes;  3.1.2 Located in designated areas;  3.1.3 Constructed of impervious material which can be readily cleaned and sanitized;  3.1.4 Made up of lids which are closed when not in immediate use  3.1.5 Segregated in a demarcated area where the waste may pose a risk to the product.  4.0  Waste management and removal 4.1 Liquid waste from toilet facilities and the main amenities are channeled into a septic tank. This is regularly recovered and disposed of by a 3rd party liquid waste management contractor.  4.2 Solid waste is segregated on a daily basis into general waste, PE waste for recycling, flexible waste for disfiguration and destruction, trim waste, plastic and others. The PE, trim waste and flexible film waste are disposed in plastic bags. Special bins that are durable to hold the various kinds of waste identified are positioned at areas where waste is generated.  4.3 The organization ensures that waste is not allowed to accumulate in product-handling or storage areas. All bins across the site are clearly labelled with the type of waste it carries.   Bins positioned at production areas and the warehouses are removed at least once per shift or when they are full, whichever comes first.  4.4 A dedicated area at the back of the factory premises has been allocated where all empty drums used in the factory are stored prior to been carted away for disposal.   4.5 A waste management service has been contracted to remove waste from the main waste area as at when due or as deemed necessary. Records of waste removal is kept.  4.6 All labelled materials, products or printed packaging materials are disfigured by cutting into shreds before disposal to ensure they cannot be reused or enter the supply chain again.  4.7 Plastic waste containing PE are disposed to a contractor for recycling. Recycled plastic materials are not used on site at any stage of production. Records of all such disposals are kept.  5.0 Drains and drainage 5.1 All drains on site have been designed, constructed and located to prevent the risk of contamination of materials and products.  5.2 Drains have been constructed according to expected flow loads and constructed away from processing lines.  5.3 The direction of flow of drains constructed does not allow a backflow to clean areas.  5.4 There are no drains within the production shop floor and process areas.   6.0 Cleaning Schedule A cleaning schedule is in place for all drains and waste bins. |  | Health Safety & Environment Officer |  |  | FS/PRP 08/CL02.004 – General Cleaning Monitoring Sheets/Waste Bins    FS/PRP 04.01 – Waste Removal Contract for External Consultant. Drain Cleaning Checklist |  |  | Microbial contamination from pests. | Waste containers must be dedicated, secured and covered. Surroundings of waste containers must be kept clean to control pests. Food packaging handlers are exempt from waste disposal. |

| 4 | Waste Disposal | PRP for Waste Disposal | The purpose of this PRP is to outline the procedure for managing waste on site to maintain a sanitary/clean environment necessary for the production of products of the highest quality and safety. | 1.0 General requirements Poly Products Ltd has put systems in place to ensure that waste materials are identified, collected, removed and disposed in a manner which prevents contamination of products and production areas.  2.0 Types of Waste The types of waste generated at Poly Products Ltd are categorized as; 2.1 Plastic waste-flexible films 2.2 General waste including packages of consumables, food debris from canteen and other office supplies 2.3 Liquid waste from toilet facilities and the main amenities.    3.0 Containers for waste, inedible or hazardous substances 3.1 The following standards and guidelines are put in place regarding containers for waste and inedible or hazardous substances:  3.1.1 Containers are clearly identified for their various intended purposes;  3.1.2 Located in designated areas;  3.1.3 Constructed of impervious material which can be readily cleaned and sanitized;  3.1.4 Made up of lids which are closed when not in immediate use  3.1.5 Segregated in a demarcated area where the waste may pose a risk to the product.  4.0  Waste management and removal 4.1 Liquid waste from toilet facilities and the main amenities are channeled into a septic tank. This is regularly recovered and disposed of by a 3rd party liquid waste management contractor.  4.2 Solid waste is segregated on a daily basis into general waste, PE waste for recycling, flexible waste for disfiguration and destruction, trim waste, plastic and others. The PE, trim waste and flexible film waste are disposed in plastic bags. Special bins that are durable to hold the various kinds of waste identified are positioned at areas where waste is generated.  4.3 The organization ensures that waste is not allowed to accumulate in product-handling or storage areas. All bins across the site are clearly labelled with the type of waste it carries.   Bins positioned at production areas and the warehouses are removed at least once per shift or when they are full, whichever comes first.  4.4 A dedicated area at the back of the factory premises has been allocated where all empty drums used in the factory are stored prior to been carted away for disposal.   4.5 A waste management service has been contracted to remove waste from the main waste area as at when due or as deemed necessary. Records of waste removal is kept.  4.6 All labelled materials, products or printed packaging materials are disfigured by cutting into shreds before disposal to ensure they cannot be reused or enter the supply chain again.  4.7 Plastic waste containing PE are disposed to a contractor for recycling. Recycled plastic materials are not used on site at any stage of production. Records of all such disposals are kept.  5.0 Drains and drainage 5.1 All drains on site have been designed, constructed and located to prevent the risk of contamination of materials and products.  5.2 Drains have been constructed according to expected flow loads and constructed away from processing lines.  5.3 The direction of flow of drains constructed does not allow a backflow to clean areas.  5.4 There are no drains within the production shop floor and process areas.   6.0 Cleaning Schedule A cleaning schedule is in place for all drains and waste bins. |  | Health Safety & Environment Officer |  |  | FS/PRP 08/CL02.004 – General Cleaning Monitoring Sheets/Waste Bins    FS/PRP 04.01 – Waste Removal Contract for External Consultant. Drain Cleaning Checklist |  |  | Microbial contamination from pests. | Waste containers must be dedicated, secured and covered. Surroundings of waste containers must be kept clean to control pests. Food packaging handlers are exempt from waste disposal. |

| FS_PRP_11 | PRP for Rework | This PRP details the actions to be taken once it is established, or suspected, that product does not meet the required standards for distribution and hence sale of a product. | Deliberate action must be taken to ensure that non-conforming food packaging meet all established food safety standards prior to release. | 7.1  General Requirements Rework is stored, handled and used in such a way that product safety, quality, traceability and regulatory compliance are maintained.  7.2 Rework can be of three main types: 7.2.1 Out of specification product 7.2.2 In specification product that needs to be re-packed 7.2.3 Product/Trade returns  7.3  Out of Specification Product 7.3.1 This is typically products that has issues with product safety or quality. This could happen to intermediate or finished goods that analysis shows that one or more critical parameters are off. Such parameters may include out of specification of critical quality parameters.  7.3.2 In the case of quality parameters or suspected microbiological contamination, the product is taken through a segregation process to sort out the compliant material from those that cannot be used for production.  The non-conforming material that cannot be re-worked is affixed with a Reject label and scrapped by cutting into shreds so as to disfigure the materials before been disposed of.  7.4 In Specification Product 7.4.1 Rework can also be generated with products that are within specification but the following may put the product into a rework category. i. Ink-stained finished food packaging ii. issues with the secondary packaging that does not affect the quality and safety of the finished primary food packaging inside. iii. illegible packaging print iv. Poor printing of images and text on finished packaging after a huge quantity has been produced and packed.  7.4.2 In the instance where there are flashes, illegible printing and poor printing of images and text, move all the affected boxes of products to the rework area.  7.4.3 The rework operator shall observe full hygiene rules in the rework area.   7.4.4 The rework operator will then sort the packaging that conforms to standards from the non-conforming products.  7.4.5 The products that conform are then repacked for final inspection by Quality Control whilst the non-conforming products is affixed with a Reject label and scrapped by cutting into shreds so as to disfigure the materials before been disposed of.  7.4.6 Quality Control then releases the conforming products   7.4.7 Rework of finished primary packaging is high risk from a hygiene perspective and must be handled to an agreed strict hygiene protocol.   7.5 Product Returns  7.5.1 Product returns can fall into two main categories 7.5.1.1 Clean trade returns 7.5.1.2 Dirty trade returns such as accident goods and in some cases badly managed packaging.  7.5.2 On arrival of trade returns, QC does a detailed inspection and classifies the returns into clean trade returns and dirty trade returns.  7.5.3 Products that are clean and not damaged are repacked into new secondary packaging under strict hygienic standards.   7.5.4 Secondary packaging are labelled to reflect the manufacturing dates and stocked at the Finished Goods warehouse for dispatch to customers.  7.5.5 Those products with defaced images and text would be affixed with a Reject label and scrapped by cutting into shreds so as to disfigure the materials before been disposed of.  7.5.6 Records of rework shall be kept and all batches with reworked packaging incorporated shall be noted for tracking purposes. | Daily | Rework Operator, Factory Manager, Quality Manager | Rework records, Disposal records. | Jewelry, hair pieces, dust and soil | 2 | Layout & Workspace | PRP for Layout & Workspace | This PRP outlines the type of layout used in putting up the facility and consideration given to workspace for employees, machinery and process flow to ensure production of safe food packaging. | 1.0 General requirements 1.1 Poly Products has the internal layouts of its facility designed, constructed and maintained to facilitate good hygiene and manufacturing practices.  1.2 The movement pattern of materials, products and people, and the layout of equipment has been designed to protect against potential contamination sources.  2.0 Internal design, layout and traffic patterns 2.1 The building has been designed to provide adequate space, with a logical flow of materials, products and personnel.  2.2 There is a physical separation of raw and packaging materials from processed areas.  2.3 All openings and paths created for the transfer of materials have been designed to minimize entry of foreign matter and pests.  3.0 Internal structures and fittings 3.1 Walls and floors in the process areas are washable and cleanable in order to prevent ingress of physical and microbiological hazards into the product.  3.2 All materials used for construction are resistant to the cleaning system applied to each area.  3.3 The facility has floor junctions and corners to facilitate cleaning. The floor has been designed in such a way to prevent standing water. There are no drains within the factory operations.  3.4 The ceilings have been designed to minimize build-up of dirt and condensation.  3.5 All external windows, and vents do not open directly into production areas and where they open into the production areas they are adequately screened.  3.6 All external opening doors are always kept closed except when otherwise needed as occasion demands.  4.0 Location of equipment 4.1 All equipment has been hygienically designed and located so as to facilitate good hygiene practices and monitoring.  4.2 Adequate space has been left around equipment to permit access for operation, cleaning and maintenance.  4.3 All direct product contact equipment is made of food contact material that can withstand sanitizing solutions at their maximum concentrations.  5.0 Laboratory facilities 5.1 All test facilities, both in-line and on-line are controlled to minimize risk of product contamination.  5.2 Poly Products Limited has designed and positioned the laboratory in such a way to prevent contamination of people, plant and products.  5.3 Microbiological assessment of products, air and other items are outsourced to the national laboratory or approved/recognized testing laboratory e.g. Ghana Standards Authority (which is accredited to ISO 17020:2012 -Conformity assessment- Requirements for the operation of various types of bodies performing inspection), SGS Laboratory etc. to prevent any risk to plant, people and products.  6.0 Temporary or mobile structures 6.1 All temporary structures would be designed, located and constructed to avoid pest harbourage and potential contamination of products. In this particular case, additional hazards associated with temporary structures would be assessed and controlled.  7.0 Storage of food raw, packaging materials and non-food chemicals 7.1 Poly Products Limited has demarcated facilities for the storage of raw, packaging materials and products. These areas are protected from dust, condensation, waste and other sources of contamination.  7.2 The storage areas are kept dry and well ventilated. Temperature monitoring is done for all storage areas.  7.3 The storage areas have been designed to allow segregation of raw materials, work in progress and finished products. 7.4 All food contact packaging finished goods will be stored on plastic pallets with the exception of incoming bulk materials (which are already stored on wooden pallets), other non-food contact materials are stored off the floor on wooden pallets and with sufficient space between the material and the walls to allow for inspection and pest control activities to be carried out.  7.5 The storage areas are designed to allow for maintenance and cleaning, the prevention of contamination and minimization of deterioration.  7.6 Solvents, chemicals and other hazardous substances are suitably labelled and segregated in areas within which liquid chemicals should be stored to ensure spillage and leakages are contained. | Daily, monthly and anualy | Maintenance manager, Food Safety Team Leader and Warehouse Supervisor | FS/PRP 02.01 – Building Layout       FS/PRP 01/CL 01 -Facility Inspection Checklist/Report  FS/PRP 08/ATTACH 01 - Cleaning Master Plan | Dust and soil particles | Chemical contamination from lubricants, cleaning detergents, solvents, etc. | Sealing or closing of accesses and openings, use of air-conditioning, regular cleaning. | 3 | Utilities | PRP for Utilities. | The PRP outlines the programmes that ensures that the organization is operating, maintaining and repairing components of the utility system to avoid contamination of products and to achieve efficiency in energy, water and air use. | 1.0 General Provisions 1.1 All factory buildings and facilities including utilities is managed in such a manner as to prevent contamination of products and processes. They are also managed in the most energy efficient manner without endangering the health and safety of employees.  1.2 Facilities Management will endeavour to take the necessary steps to provide an adequate, reliable, and cost-effective utilities infrastructure at all present and planned future buildings and facilities managed by the department. These shall be established in the most hygienic manner in order to ensure product safety.  1.3 The provision and distribution routes for utilities to and around processing and storage areas are designed to minimize the risk of product contamination. The quality of utilities is monitored to minimize product contamination risk.   2.0 Water Supply 2.1 Sufficient supply of potable water to meet the needs of production processes is assured. Facilities for storage and distribution of water have been designed to meet the quality requirements of water.  2.2 Poly Products uses water for washing and other cleaning activities. Potable water is sourced from the municipal water treatment plant. Approved water pipes have been used on site to connect water from the main municipal lines to preserve its quality and safety. Connections are hygienically done to prevent external contaminated water from flowing into the pipes in the event that water stops flowing from the treatment plant.  2.3 Periodic water analysis shall be done on an annual basis. See attachment FS/PRP 03/ATTACH 01 for the scope, frequency, sampling point etc. This activity is outsourced to the national laboratory or approved/recognized testing laboratory to carry out by taking water. The appropriate ISO method or other authorized standard for air count is employed in this exercise.   3.0 Air quality and ventilation 3.1 Air flowing from outside into the production space can be a source of bacteria and mould spores. Poly Products has considered this in the design of its ventilation system especially at the production hall. Hence there are no windows opening directly into the production areas.  3.2 Periodic air counts are done for each of the sections of production. See attachment FS/PRP 03/ATTACH 01 This activity is outsourced to the national laboratory or approved/recognized testing laboratory to carry out. Prepared media in petri dishes are exposed in various sections of production for some minutes. Dishes are incubated and the total viable count results are analyzed. The appropriate ISO method or other authorized standard for air count is employed in this exercise.   4.0 Compressed air and other gases 4.1 Compressed air (which are from in-built vacuum pumps) used in the production process have been constructed and maintained so as to prevent direct contact products and the packaging.  4.2 Maintenance of the compressed air system is part of the site maintenance schedule. Maintenance shall include checking and cleaning of filters and replacement of filters if necessary.   5.0 Lighting 5.1 Adequate lighting has been provided in all production and storage areas to allow personnel to operate in a hygienic manner.   5.2 All lights in both critical and non-critical areas are covered to catch fragments of glass in case of lamp breakage.   5.3 Maintenance work on lighting is done in such a way as to prevent contamination of products. Light bulb replacement shall be done during weekend shutdown maintenance periods and not in the course of production.  5.4 Indoor lighting will be reduced in number and / or wattage, wherever possible, to provide for the minimum but adequate lighting levels consistent with the needs of the programs and functions being provided in those spaces, and with any state-mandated standards for the efficient and effective use of those spaces.  5.5 For efficient use of energy, the rooftop including production and storage areas are equipped with transparent roof for sunlight illumination during daytime.   5.6 Outside lighting on building exteriors and loading bay shall be maintained at the brightness levels necessary to provide appropriate security and safety on the facility’s grounds, parking lots, and building entrances. | Daily, weekly, monthly, etc. | Maintenance Manager, Factory Manager, Food Safety Team Leade and Departmental heads. | FS/PRP 03/ATTACH 01 - Plan/Schedule for Water, Air, Swab Analysis | Dust and soil contamination from environment. |  | Microbial contamination form air and water. site plans and processing details are controlled. 7.2.3 Personnel Security Measures 7.2.3.1 Personnel security is taken seriously. Measures have been put in place to ensure that only authorized personnel are on the factory premises at any point in time. This includes visitors on site. 7.2.3.2 This establishment has in place at least one of the following measures for personnel security; 7.2.3.2.1 Employee Security 7.2.3.2.1.1 During hiring of employees, thorough background checks are done. 7.2.3.2.1.2 Employees are trained to know what they can do on site. 7.2.3.2.1.3 Areas restricted to be accessed by only a category of employees is made known to every employee hired. 7.2.3.2.1.4 Confidentiality clauses are inserted into employment letters. Employees are made to sign the confidentiality agreement. 7.2.3.2.2 Non-employee Security 7.2.3.2.2.1 Provision has been made for non-employees such as visitors, guests, customers, contractors, suppliers, third party drivers etc. 7.2.3.2.2.2 A log of non-employees entering the establishment is maintained at the main security area. 7.2.3.2.2.3 A visitor’s ID card has been designed with numbers and these are assigned to every visitor who enters the facility to conduct one business or the other. 7.2.3.2.2.4 All visitors are mandated to wear their visitor ID cards where they would be very visible. 7.2.3.2.2.5 Non-employees are chaperoned on-site by security or the person they came to transact business with and they are basically restricted to designated areas of the factory. 7.2.3.2.2.6 Non-employees have restrictions on what they can do on site. For instance, non-employees are not permitted to take pictures on site. 7.2.3.2.3 Security Training 7.2.3.2.3.1 All new employees undergo security awareness training. Existing employees undergo periodic security awareness training. 7.2.3.2.3.2 Employees are trained on access control, handling of sensitive information, what suspicious activities look like and reporting such activities to management or the security team. 7.2.4 Incident Response Security Measures. 7.2.4.1 An incident response security references the incident management plan already in place. The idea is to respond quickly to a product contamination threat or event using planned measures. 7.2.4.2 There is already an existing incident management plan which deals with product recalls whether it is food safety related or quality

| FS_PRP_06 | Management of Purchased materials and services | This PRP describes the selection of suppliers for the supply of the types of raw and packaging materials purchased for production and how they are received and stored in the factory. | Procurement of materials and services for use in production must be managed in order to control food safety risks to food packing. | 1.0 Selection and management of suppliers 1.1.1 To ensure the right supplier is selected a hazard assessment, including the potential risk to the final product is used to justify the decision to engage a particular supplier.  1.1.2 The following is done; 1.1.2.1 Assess the supplier’s ability to meet quality and food safety expectations, requirements and specifications.  1.1.2.2 Some of the procedures used for assessing suppliers include; 1.1.2.2.1 Audit of the supplying site prior to accepting materials for production or the provision of relevant certifications or desktop audit.  1.1.2.2.2 Appropriate third-party certification.  1.1.2.2.3 Performance monitoring of the supplier to assure continued approval status. 1.1.2.2.4 Suppliers will be contacted on their performance and be required to reply especially to non-conformances that involves product quality  1.2 Incoming material requirements (raw/ingredients/packaging) 1.2.1 All delivery vehicles are checked prior to, and during, offloading to verify that the quality and safety of the material has been maintained during transit.  1.2.2 All delivered materials are tested and or covered by COA to verify conformity with specified requirements prior to acceptance or use. The method of verification is documented for each item delivered by suppliers.  1.3.3 The inspection frequency is based on the hazard presented by the material and the risk assessment of the specific suppliers.  1.3.4 All non-conforming products are placed on-hold and rejected to be returned back to the supplier. 1.3.5 In cases where purchased items are imported, the supplier is notified of the non-conformance after which the material is either sold to recycling plants in the case of packaging or destroyed under supervision in the case of other items which cannot be recycled. 1.3.6 Criteria for disqualification: 1.3.6.1 Lack of prompt response to complaint or problem identify by the suppliers. 1.3.6.2 Lack of supply of quality raw material in two successions without corrective actions.  1.3.7 All items purchased are stored in demarcated storage areas and released to production for use. | Daily, monthly and anually | Factory Manager, Warehouse Manager, | FS/PRP 06/REC 05 - Approved Suppliers and Service Providers' List  Material Intake Checklist                  FS/PRP 06/FORM 01 – Supplier Monitoring/Tracking sheet     FS/PRP 06/FORM 02 -  Suppliers/Questionnaire Evaluation Form Internal Audit Reports |  | Chemical contamination |  | Procedure for handling and storing food and non-food materials. |

  PPL PRPs

| FS_PRP_06 | Management of Purchased materials and services | This PRP describes the selection of suppliers for the supply of the types of raw and packaging materials purchased for production and how they are received and stored in the factory. | Procurement of materials and services for use in production must be managed in order to control food safety risks to food packing. | 1.0 Selection and management of suppliers 1.1.1 To ensure the right supplier is selected a hazard assessment, including the potential risk to the final product is used to justify the decision to engage a particular supplier.  1.1.2 The following is done; 1.1.2.1 Assess the supplier’s ability to meet quality and food safety expectations, requirements and specifications.  1.1.2.2 Some of the procedures used for assessing suppliers include; 1.1.2.2.1 Audit of the supplying site prior to accepting materials for production or the provision of relevant certifications or desktop audit.  1.1.2.2.2 Appropriate third-party certification.  1.1.2.2.3 Performance monitoring of the supplier to assure continued approval status. 1.1.2.2.4 Suppliers will be contacted on their performance and be required to reply especially to non-conformances that involves product quality  1.2 Incoming material requirements (raw/ingredients/packaging) 1.2.1 All delivery vehicles are checked prior to, and during, offloading to verify that the quality and safety of the material has been maintained during transit.  1.2.2 All delivered materials are tested and or covered by COA to verify conformity with specified requirements prior to acceptance or use. The method of verification is documented for each item delivered by suppliers.  1.3.3 The inspection frequency is based on the hazard presented by the material and the risk assessment of the specific suppliers.  1.3.4 All non-conforming products are placed on-hold and rejected to be returned back to the supplier. 1.3.5 In cases where purchased items are imported, the supplier is notified of the non-conformance after which the material is either sold to recycling plants in the case of packaging or destroyed under supervision in the case of other items which cannot be recycled. 1.3.6 Criteria for disqualification: 1.3.6.1 Lack of prompt response to complaint or problem identify by the suppliers. 1.3.6.2 Lack of supply of quality raw material in two successions without corrective actions.  1.3.7 All items purchased are stored in demarcated storage areas and released to production for use. | Daily, monthly and anually | Factory Manager, Warehouse Manager, | FS/PRP 06/REC 05 - Approved Suppliers and Service Providers' List  Material Intake Checklist                  FS/PRP 06/FORM 01 – Supplier Monitoring/Tracking sheet     FS/PRP 06/FORM 02 -  Suppliers/Questionnaire Evaluation Form Internal Audit Reports |  | Chemical contamination |  | Procedure for handling and storing food and non-food materials. |

||
site plans and processing details are controlled. 7.2.3 Personnel Security Measures 7.2.3.1 Personnel security is taken seriously. Measures have been put in place to ensure that only authorized personnel are on the factory premises at any point in time. This includes visitors on site. 7.2.3.2 This establishment has in place at least one of the following measures for personnel security; 7.2.3.2.1 Employee Security 7.2.3.2.1.1 During hiring of employees, thorough background checks are done. 7.2.3.2.1.2 Employees are trained to know what they can do on site. 7.2.3.2.1.3 Areas restricted to be accessed by only a category of employees is made known to every employee hired. 7.2.3.2.1.4 Confidentiality clauses are inserted into employment letters. Employees are made to sign the confidentiality agreement. 7.2.3.2.2 Non-employee Security 7.2.3.2.2.1 Provision has been made for non-employees such as visitors, guests, customers, contractors, suppliers, third party drivers etc. 7.2.3.2.2.2 A log of non-employees entering the establishment is maintained at the main security area. 7.2.3.2.2.3 A visitor’s ID card has been designed with numbers and these are assigned to every visitor who enters the facility to conduct one business or the other. 7.2.3.2.2.4 All visitors are mandated to wear their visitor ID cards where they would be very visible. 7.2.3.2.2.5 Non-employees are chaperoned on-site by security or the person they came to transact business with and they are basically restricted to designated areas of the factory. 7.2.3.2.2.6 Non-employees have restrictions on what they can do on site. For instance, non-employees are not permitted to take pictures on site. 7.2.3.2.3 Security Training 7.2.3.2.3.1 All new employees undergo security awareness training. Existing employees undergo periodic security awareness training. 7.2.3.2.3.2 Employees are trained on access control, handling of sensitive information, what suspicious activities look like and reporting such activities to management or the security team. 7.2.4 Incident Response Security Measures. 7.2.4.1 An incident response security references the incident management plan already in place. The idea is to respond quickly to a product contamination threat or event using planned measures. 7.2.4.2 There is already an existing incident management plan which deals with product recalls whether it is food safety related or quality

| Food Fraud | This Program is designed to assess put in place Economically-Motivated adulteration of food products and put in place proportional control meausres | GOPDC FSQM has considered all possible threats and has established threat assesment critical control points (TACCP). This also provides guidance on the avoidance and mitigation of threat to food and food supply. The possible risk associated with this Program includes: destruction of equipment and machinery,pilfering, intruders, delibrate contamination of food, fraud, extortion of money, attack by poachers, cyber crime, personnel security and disgrutled individual tampering , closing down the factory and food incident cases. | GOPDC has adopted Threat Assesment Critical Control points (TACCP)approach according to PAS 965: 2014 and has a team (trained security operatives and Food Safety Team), access control measures, survellance team, material and vehicle movement control documents, key registers. Also deployment of armed security personnel to vulnerable points, internal police post, issuing of visitors reflective jackets and documentation, changing facilities - seperate personal clothing from work wear and possitive identification of staff. Demacation and sign post have also been installed at restricted areas to control movement of persons. We also have corrective measures to tampering evidence ( seals on trucks), fire extinquisher installed all round the premises and offices to control fire outbreak. There is training of recruited security personnel on access control of people and vehicles in and out of the factory. Related necessary plans/procedures such as product recalls/withdrawals and personnel emergency or evacuation procedures are in place and effective Employees, contractors as well as visitors are identified by appropriate form of ID card or other appropriate means (Reflectors) The factory is securely fenced to prevent unauthorized entry of people and vehicles. There is placement of notices at the security gate or entrance which will direct visitors and unauthorized persons into the factory (visitors’ policy). Security cameras are in placed at high security risk areas in the factory eg. Refinery stearin melting tanks, filling plant, warehouses, product storage tanks, water treatment and where applicable continuous monitoring by an attendant and/or a security personnel. There is one entrance for authorized

site plans and processing details are controlled. 7.2.3 Personnel Security Measures 7.2.3.1 Personnel security is taken seriously. Measures have been put in place to ensure that only authorized personnel are on the factory premises at any point in time. This includes visitors on site. 7.2.3.2 This establishment has in place at least one of the following measures for personnel security; 7.2.3.2.1 Employee Security 7.2.3.2.1.1 During hiring of employees, thorough background checks are done. 7.2.3.2.1.2 Employees are trained to know what they can do on site. 7.2.3.2.1.3 Areas restricted to be accessed by only a category of employees is made known to every employee hired. 7.2.3.2.1.4 Confidentiality clauses are inserted into employment letters. Employees are made to sign the confidentiality agreement. 7.2.3.2.2 Non-employee Security 7.2.3.2.2.1 Provision has been made for non-employees such as visitors, guests, customers, contractors, suppliers, third party drivers etc. 7.2.3.2.2.2 A log of non-employees entering the establishment is maintained at the main security area. 7.2.3.2.2.3 A visitor’s ID card has been designed with numbers and these are assigned to every visitor who enters the facility to conduct one business or the other. 7.2.3.2.2.4 All visitors are mandated to wear their visitor ID cards where they would be very visible. 7.2.3.2.2.5 Non-employees are chaperoned on-site by security or the person they came to transact business with and they are basically restricted to designated areas of the factory. 7.2.3.2.2.6 Non-employees have restrictions on what they can do on site. For instance, non-employees are not permitted to take pictures on site. 7.2.3.2.3 Security Training 7.2.3.2.3.1 All new employees undergo security awareness training. Existing employees undergo periodic security awareness training. 7.2.3.2.3.2 Employees are trained on access control, handling of sensitive information, what suspicious activities look like and reporting such activities to management or the security team. 7.2.4 Incident Response Security Measures. 7.2.4.1 An incident response security references the incident management plan already in place. The idea is to respond quickly to a product contamination threat or event using planned measures. 7.2.4.2 There is already an existing incident management plan which deals with product recalls whether it is food safety related or quality
  --- End Chunk #3 ---

  Scope Statement Guidance - FSMS
||
| | Guidance on Scope Wording: The certificate scope statement shall: 1) Be within the scope of the Scheme; 2) Clearly and unambiguously describe the process/activities, product types and/or services that are supplied by the certified organization and that have been auditedby the CB. The report shall contain evidence of all activities in the scope statement; 3 )Not include promotional statements or claims. Claims being any message or representation, which is not mandatory under legislation and which suggests that the food or service has particular characteristics. Examples are health claims, nutritional claims, origin claims, free-from claims (e.g. allergen free claims), organic, quality claims, as well as vegetarion or vegan; Where an organization makes such claims, they shall be investigated when they are part of the FSMS but shallnot appear in scope statement; 4)Brand names are not allowed as this might suggest product certification; 5) Be in English, but another language may be added (e.g. the native language of the country of the certified organization); 6) Not mention subcontracted or outsourced processes outside the organization’slegal responsibility; 7) Not include company names; 8) Shall not include activities such as trading, broking; 9)Not include reference to products, processes or services related to non-food/feed (e.g. shall not refer to pharmaceutical and self-medication products, tobacco, cosmetics, household and personal care, ink); 10) Not contain exclusions for activities, processes, products or services when those activities, processes, products or services can have an influence on the food safety of the end products as defined in the scope of certification (ISO/TS 22003:2013 9.1.1); Where permitted exclusions apply, this shall be motivated in the report and the certificate shall reference the exclusion as part of the scope statement ; 11) Not contain Development and Design as separate activity. These activities are only allowed when part of a processing or manufacturing activity covered by the FSSC 22000 scope of certification and part of the same legal entity. | Guidance on Scope Wording: The certificate scope statement shall: 1) Be within the scope of the Scheme; 2) Clearly and unambiguously describe the process/activities, product types and/or services that are supplied by
