Measures have been put in place to ensure that only authorized personnel are on the factory premises at any point in time. This includes visitors on site. 7.2.3.2 This establishment has in place at least one of the following measures for personnel security; 7.2.3.2.1 Employee Security 7.2.3.2.1.1 During hiring of employees, thorough background checks are done. 7.2.3.2.1.2 Employees are trained to know what they can do on site. 7.2.3.2.1.3 Areas restricted to be accessed by only a category of employees is made known to every employee hired. 7.2.3.2.1.4 Confidentiality clauses are inserted into employment letters. Employees are made to sign the confidentiality agreement. 7.2.3.2.2 Non-employee Security 7.2.3.2.2.1 Provision has been made for non-employees such as visitors, guests, customers, contractors, suppliers, third party drivers etc. 7.2.3.2.2.2 A log of non-employees entering the establishment is maintained at the main security area. 7.2.3.2.2.3 A visitor’s ID card has been designed with numbers and these are assigned to every visitor who enters the facility to conduct one business or the other. 7.2.3.2.2.4 All visitors are mandated to wear their visitor ID cards where they would be very visible. 7.2.3.2.2.5 Non-employees are chaperoned on-site by security or the person they came to transact business with and they are basically restricted to designated areas of the factory. 7.2.3.2.2.6 Non-employees have restrictions on what they can do on site. For instance, non-employees are not permitted to take pictures on site. 7.2.3.2.3 Security Training 7.2.3.2.3.1 All new employees undergo security awareness training. Existing employees undergo periodic security awareness training. 7.2.3.2.3.2 Employees are trained on access control, handling of sensitive information, what suspicious activities look like and reporting such activities to management or the security team. 7.2.4 Incident Response Security Measures. 7.2.4.1 An incident response security references the incident management plan already in place.   Scope Statement Guidance - FSMS
||
| | Additional remarks Always describe the audited processes and products / product groups. It is recommended to use terminology like processing, manufacturing, packing; Not be misleading. Not be vague. site plans and processing details are controlled. 7.2.3 Personnel Security Measures 7.2.3.1 Personnel security is taken seriously. Measures have been put in place to ensure that only authorized personnel are on the factory premises at any point in time. This includes visitors on site. 7.2.3.2 This establishment has in place at least one of the following measures for personnel security; 7.2.3.2.1 Employee Security 7.2.3.2.1.1 During hiring of employees, thorough background checks are done. 7.2.3.2.1.2 Employees are trained to know what they can do on site. 7.2.3.2.1.3 Areas restricted to be accessed by only a category of employees is made known to every employee hired. 7.2.3.2.1.4 Confidentiality clauses are inserted into employment letters. Employees are made to sign the confidentiality agreement. 7.2.3.2.2 Non-employee Security 7.2.3.2.2.1 Provision has been made for non-employees such as visitors, guests, customers, contractors, suppliers, third party drivers etc. 7.2.3.2.2.2 A log of non-employees entering the establishment is maintained at the main security area. 7.2.3.2.2.3 A visitor’s ID card has been designed with numbers and these are assigned to every visitor who enters the facility to conduct one business or the other. 7.2.3.2.2.4 All visitors are mandated to wear their visitor ID cards where they would be very visible. 7.2.3.2.2.5 Non-employees are chaperoned on-site by security or the person they came to transact business with and they are basically restricted to designated areas of the factory. 7.2.3.2.2.6 Non-employees have restrictions on what they can do on site. For instance, non-employees are not permitted to take pictures on site. 7.2.3.2.3 Security Training 7.2.3.2.3.1 All new employees undergo security awareness training. Existing employees undergo periodic security awareness training. 7.2.3.2.3.2 Employees are trained on access control, handling of sensitive information, what suspicious activities look like and reporting such activities to management or the security team. 7.2.4 Incident Response Security Measures. 7.2.4.1 An incident response security references the incident management plan already in place. The idea is to respond quickly to a product contamination threat or event using planned measures. 7.2.4.2 There is already an existing incident management plan which deals with product recalls whether it is food safety related or quality

  Text:
  Scope Statement Guidance - FSMS
||
| | Guidance on Scope Wording: The certificate scope statement shall: 1) Be within the scope of the Scheme; 2) Clearly and unambiguously describe the process/activities, product types and/or services that are supplied by the certified organization and that have been auditedby the CB. The report shall contain evidence of all activities in the scope statement; 3 )Not include promotional statements or claims. Claims being any message or representation, which is not mandatory under legislation and which suggests that the food or service has particular characteristics. Examples are health claims, nutritional claims, origin claims, free-from claims (e.g. allergen free claims), organic, quality claims, as well as vegetarion or vegan; Where an organization makes such claims, they shall be investigated when they are part of the FSMS but shallnot appear in scope statement; 4)Brand names are not allowed as this might suggest product certification; 5) Be in English, but another language may be added (e.g. the native language of the country of the certified organization); 6) Not mention subcontracted or outsourced processes outside the organization’slegal responsibility; 7) Not include company names; 8) Shall not include activities such as trading, broking; 9)Not include reference to products, processes or services related to non-food/feed (e.g. shall not refer to pharmaceutical and self-medication products, tobacco, cosmetics, household and personal care, ink); 10) Not contain exclusions for activities, processes, products or services when those activities, processes, products or services can have an influence on the food safety of the end products as defined in the scope of certification (ISO/TS 22003:2013 9.1.1); Where permitted exclusions apply, this shall be motivated in the report and the certificate shall reference the exclusion as part of the scope statement ; 11) Not contain Development and Design as separate activity. These activities are only allowed when part of a processing or manufacturing activity covered by the FSSC 22000 scope of certification and part of the same legal entity. | Guidance on Scope Wording: The certificate scope statement shall: 1) Be within the scope of the Scheme; 2) Clearly and unambiguously describe the process/activities, product types and/or services that are supplied by
  --- End Chunk #9 ---

For instance, non-employees are not permitted to take pictures on site. 7.2.3.2.3 Security Training 7.2.3.2.3.1 All new employees undergo security awareness training. Existing employees undergo periodic security awareness training. 7.2.3.2.3.2 Employees are trained on access control, handling of sensitive information, what suspicious activities look like and reporting such activities to management or the security team. 7.2.4 Incident Response Security Measures. 7.2.4.1 An incident response security references the incident management plan already in place. | Food Fraud | This Program is designed to assess put in place Economically-Motivated adulteration of food products and put in place proportional control meausres | GOPDC FSQM has considered all possible threats and has established threat assesment critical control points (TACCP). This also provides guidance on the avoidance and mitigation of threat to food and food supply. The possible risk associated with this Program includes: destruction of equipment and machinery,pilfering, intruders, delibrate contamination of food, fraud, extortion of money, attack by poachers, cyber crime, personnel security and disgrutled individual tampering , closing down the factory and food incident cases. | GOPDC has adopted Threat Assesment Critical Control points (TACCP)approach according to PAS 965: 2014 and has a team (trained security operatives and Food Safety Team), access control measures, survellance team, material and vehicle movement control documents, key registers. Also deployment of armed security personnel to vulnerable points, internal police post, issuing of visitors reflective jackets and documentation, changing facilities - seperate personal clothing from work wear and possitive identification of staff. Demacation and sign post have also been installed at restricted areas to control movement of persons. We also have corrective measures to tampering evidence ( seals on trucks), fire extinquisher installed all round the premises and offices to control fire outbreak. There is training of recruited security personnel on access control of people and vehicles in and out of the factory. Related necessary plans/procedures such as product recalls/withdrawals and personnel emergency or evacuation procedures are in place and effective Employees, contractors as well as visitors are identified by appropriate form of ID card or other appropriate means (Reflectors) The factory is securely fenced to prevent unauthorized entry of people and vehicles. There is placement of notices at the security gate or entrance which will direct visitors and unauthorized persons into the factory (visitors’ policy). Security cameras are in placed at high security risk areas in the factory eg. Refinery stearin melting tanks, filling plant, warehouses, product storage tanks, water treatment and where applicable continuous monitoring by an attendant and/or a security personnel. There is one entrance for authorized

| FS_PRP_06 | Management of Purchased materials and services | This PRP describes the selection of suppliers for the supply of the types of raw and packaging materials purchased for production and how they are received and stored in the factory. | Procurement of materials and services for use in production must be managed in order to control food safety risks to food packing. | 1.0 Selection and management of suppliers 1.1.1 To ensure the right supplier is selected a hazard assessment, including the potential risk to the final product is used to justify the decision to engage a particular supplier.  1.1.2 The following is done; 1.1.2.1 Assess the supplier’s ability to meet quality and food safety expectations, requirements and specifications.  1.1.2.2 Some of the procedures used for assessing suppliers include; 1.1.2.2.1 Audit of the supplying site prior to accepting materials for production or the provision of relevant certifications or desktop audit.  1.1.2.2.2 Appropriate third-party certification.  1.1.2.2.3 Performance monitoring of the supplier to assure continued approval status. 1.1.2.2.4 Suppliers will be contacted on their performance and be required to reply especially to non-conformances that involves product quality  1.2 Incoming material requirements (raw/ingredients/packaging) 1.2.1 All delivery vehicles are checked prior to, and during, offloading to verify that the quality and safety of the material has been maintained during transit.  1.2.2 All delivered materials are tested and or covered by COA to verify conformity with specified requirements prior to acceptance or use. The method of verification is documented for each item delivered by suppliers.  1.3.3 The inspection frequency is based on the hazard presented by the material and the risk assessment of the specific suppliers.  1.3.4 All non-conforming products are placed on-hold and rejected to be returned back to the supplier. 1.3.5 In cases where purchased items are imported, the supplier is notified of the non-conformance after which the material is either sold to recycling plants in the case of packaging or destroyed under supervision in the case of other items which cannot be recycled. 1.3.6 Criteria for disqualification: 1.3.6.1 Lack of prompt response to complaint or problem identify by the suppliers. 1.3.6.2 Lack of supply of quality raw material in two successions without corrective actions.  1.3.7 All items purchased are stored in demarcated storage areas and released to production for use. | Daily, monthly and anually | Factory Manager, Warehouse Manager, | FS/PRP 06/REC 05 - Approved Suppliers and Service Providers' List  Material Intake Checklist                  FS/PRP 06/FORM 01 – Supplier Monitoring/Tracking sheet     FS/PRP 06/FORM 02 -  Suppliers/Questionnaire Evaluation Form Internal Audit Reports |  | Chemical contamination |  | Procedure for handling and storing food and non-food materials. |

| FS_PRP_06 | Management of Purchased materials and services | This PRP describes the selection of suppliers for the supply of the types of raw and packaging materials purchased for production and how they are received and stored in the factory. | Procurement of materials and services for use in production must be managed in order to control food safety risks to food packing. | 1.0 Selection and management of suppliers 1.1.1 To ensure the right supplier is selected a hazard assessment, including the potential risk to the final product is used to justify the decision to engage a particular supplier.  1.1.2 The following is done; 1.1.2.1 Assess the supplier’s ability to meet quality and food safety expectations, requirements and specifications.  1.1.2.2 Some of the procedures used for assessing suppliers include; 1.1.2.2.1 Audit of the supplying site prior to accepting materials for production or the provision of relevant certifications or desktop audit.  1.1.2.2.2 Appropriate third-party certification.  1.1.2.2.3 Performance monitoring of the supplier to assure continued approval status. 1.1.2.2.4 Suppliers will be contacted on their performance and be required to reply especially to non-conformances that involves product quality  1.2 Incoming material requirements (raw/ingredients/packaging) 1.2.1 All delivery vehicles are checked prior to, and during, offloading to verify that the quality and safety of the material has been maintained during transit.  1.2.2 All delivered materials are tested and or covered by COA to verify conformity with specified requirements prior to acceptance or use. The method of verification is documented for each item delivered by suppliers.  1.3.3 The inspection frequency is based on the hazard presented by the material and the risk assessment of the specific suppliers.  1.3.4 All non-conforming products are placed on-hold and rejected to be returned back to the supplier. 1.3.5 In cases where purchased items are imported, the supplier is notified of the non-conformance after which the material is either sold to recycling plants in the case of packaging or destroyed under supervision in the case of other items which cannot be recycled. 1.3.6 Criteria for disqualification: 1.3.6.1 Lack of prompt response to complaint or problem identify by the suppliers. 1.3.6.2 Lack of supply of quality raw material in two successions without corrective actions.  1.3.7 All items purchased are stored in demarcated storage areas and released to production for use. | Daily, monthly and anually | Factory Manager, Warehouse Manager, | FS/PRP 06/REC 05 - Approved Suppliers and Service Providers' List  Material Intake Checklist                  FS/PRP 06/FORM 01 – Supplier Monitoring/Tracking sheet     FS/PRP 06/FORM 02 -  Suppliers/Questionnaire Evaluation Form Internal Audit Reports |  | Chemical contamination |  | Procedure for handling and storing food and non-food materials. |

| FS_PRP_11 | PRP for Rework | This PRP details the actions to be taken once it is established, or suspected, that product does not meet the required standards for distribution and hence sale of a product. | Deliberate action must be taken to ensure that non-conforming food packaging meet all established food safety standards prior to release. | 7.1  General Requirements Rework is stored, handled and used in such a way that product safety, quality, traceability and regulatory compliance are maintained.  7.2 Rework can be of three main types: 7.2.1 Out of specification product 7.2.2 In specification product that needs to be re-packed 7.2.3 Product/Trade returns  7.3  Out of Specification Product 7.3.1 This is typically products that has issues with product safety or quality. This could happen to intermediate or finished goods that analysis shows that one or more critical parameters are off. Such parameters may include out of specification of critical quality parameters.  7.3.2 In the case of quality parameters or suspected microbiological contamination, the product is taken through a segregation process to sort out the compliant material from those that cannot be used for production.  The non-conforming material that cannot be re-worked is affixed with a Reject label and scrapped by cutting into shreds so as to disfigure the materials before been disposed of.  7.4 In Specification Product 7.4.1 Rework can also be generated with products that are within specification but the following may put the product into a rework category. i. Ink-stained finished food packaging ii. issues with the secondary packaging that does not affect the quality and safety of the finished primary food packaging inside. iii. illegible packaging print iv. Poor printing of images and text on finished packaging after a huge quantity has been produced and packed.  7.4.2 In the instance where there are flashes, illegible printing and poor printing of images and text, move all the affected boxes of products to the rework area.  7.4.3 The rework operator shall observe full hygiene rules in the rework area.   7.4.4 The rework operator will then sort the packaging that conforms to standards from the non-conforming products.  7.4.5 The products that conform are then repacked for final inspection by Quality Control whilst the non-conforming products is affixed with a Reject label and scrapped by cutting into shreds so as to disfigure the materials before been disposed of.  7.4.6 Quality Control then releases the conforming products   7.4.7 Rework of finished primary packaging is high risk from a hygiene perspective and must be handled to an agreed strict hygiene protocol.   7.5 Product Returns  7.5.1 Product returns can fall into two main categories 7.5.1.1 Clean trade returns 7.5.1.2 Dirty trade returns such as accident goods and in some cases badly managed packaging.  7.5.2 On arrival of trade returns, QC does a detailed inspection and classifies the returns into clean trade returns and dirty trade returns.  7.5.3 Products that are clean and not damaged are repacked into new secondary packaging under strict hygienic standards.   7.5.4 Secondary packaging are labelled to reflect the manufacturing dates and stocked at the Finished Goods warehouse for dispatch to customers.  7.5.5 Those products with defaced images and text would be affixed with a Reject label and scrapped by cutting into shreds so as to disfigure the materials before been disposed of.  7.5.6 Records of rework shall be kept and all batches with reworked | FS_PRP_05 | Equipment Suitability, Cleaning & Maintenance | PRP for Equipement Suitabilty, Cleaning & Maintenance | The purpose of this PRP is to ensure that equipment used in production and packaging areas are designed to prevent contamination | 1.0 General Requirements 1.1 Poly Products Company Limited has provided equipment designed to prevent contamination for use in production of food packaging.  2.0  Hygiene Design and food contact surfaces 2.1 Poly Products Company Limited has taken into consideration the potential sources of contamination from equipment constructed with unsuitable material. 2.2 Therefore, all processing equipment are constructed from stainless steel and firm non-leaking and non-wearable plastic material. The construction materials compatible with the intended food packaging, lubricants and cleaning or flushing agents. 2.3 The food contact surfaces of the processing equipment are smooth, accessible and cleanable.  2.4  Equipment components containing metals of known toxicity (e.g. mercury) are excluded from use for the processing of food packaging.  3.0 Maintenance of Equipment  3.1 Poly Products Company Limited has in place a system of planned maintenance which covers all equipment.  3.2 Equipment maintenance programmes are available and systematically applied to minimize the potential for contamination of product by equipment.  3.3 A procedure has been established to remove any potential contaminant from machinery and equipment after maintenance work. Equipment with product contact surfaces after maintenance are released in accordance to line release protocols before being used by production.    3.4 Maintenance personnel are required to follow the prescribed procedures including, where appropriate, hygiene measures. Temporary engineering and modifications are avoided but strictly controlled when they are carried out. | Daily | Maintenance Engineer Food Safety Team Leader Factory Manager | FS/PRP05.01 – Equipment Calibration Schedule    FS/PRP 05.03 – Equipment Cleaning Record    FS_PRP_05 ATTACH 01 – Preventive Maintenance Plan    FS/PRP 01/CL 01 -Facility Inspection Checklist/Report    FS/PRP04.02 – Job Ticket    FS/PRP06/ATTACH01 – Stock Card | Dust and soil particles from environment. | Chemical contamination from lubricants, fuels and detergents. | Microbial contamination from personnel. | GMP protocols for personnel, cleaning and maintenance of equipment, pest control program, use of food grade lubricants and detergents. |
